title: A SIP is a habit, not a product
objectives: Explain why the decisions after a SIP starts matter more than the product itself.
Name the five L.E.A.R.N. stages of this module.
State the one line to remember.
body_md:
A mutual fund SIP is not a product you sell once. It is a habit a client keeps for ten or twenty years, and most of its value comes from decisions made after the first instalment.

## Where the value is

- Starting a SIP takes ten minutes. Guiding it takes two decades.
- The decisions are predictable: step up, pause, missed debit, market fall, end date, goal near, goal reached.
- Each one has a default answer, and the default is often the opposite of what the client asks for in the moment.

## How this module runs

This module follows the same L.E.A.R.N. framework as the rest of the series.

- Learn: the SIP life cycle, and the rules that govern it.
- Evaluate: four checks and six client sentences before any change.
- Act right: what to do at each stage, from renewal to withdrawal.
- Review: a 20-minute annual review that replaces ten panicked calls.
- Navigate: the behaviour that breaks SIPs, and the words that steady it.

**The one line to remember:** a SIP is a habit, not a product. Our job is to protect the habit.
example: A client has run a ₹10,000 SIP for nine years and asks whether to stop it now that the tenure is nearly over. The habit, not the scheme form, is what built the corpus — so the conversation starts with the goal date, not with the end date.
say: Selling the SIP is the start of our work, not the end of it.
Most of the value we add comes from the decisions after the first instalment.
never: Your SIP will take care of itself now.
Just keep paying and don't ask questions.

check.q: What is a SIP best described as, for the purpose of this module?
o: A one-time product to be sold
A habit that has to be protected for years
check.why: A SIP is a habit, not a product: the value comes from the decisions made after the first instalment.

check.q: Which is NOT one of the module's five L.E.A.R.N. stages?
check.why: The stages are Learn, Evaluate, Act right, Review and rebalance, and Navigate behaviour. Forecasting the market is never one of them.

check.q: Who is this module written for?
o: New employees, the sales team, and investors as awareness material
check.why: The module is training and investor awareness material for the whole team.
